title: Duplicate Listing Detection Across Portals

blueprintSignals.name: Address match
blueprintSignals.definition: normalised and geocoded address equality with unit number retained
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Formats differ between portals, so normalise before comparing

blueprintSignals.name: Image hash similarity
blueprintSignals.definition: smallest perceptual-hash distance between any pair of photos across two listings
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Re-edited and cropped images change the hash, so back it with an embedding match

blueprintSignals.name: Price and size agreement
blueprintSignals.definition: relative difference in asking price and in floor area against a tolerance
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Prices change between portals within days, so use a tolerance not equality

blueprintSignals.name: Agent relation
blueprintSignals.definition: whether the two listings come from the same broker or agency
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Data on agency relationships is incomplete

engineFeatures.meaning: how many entities share each linking value, so a value shared by three says more than one shared by three hundred
how many different kinds of value two records share
character-level overlap of the two names, tolerant of typos

engineFeatures.feature: group size of the rarest shared value
engineFeatures.meaning: log of the size of the smallest group the pair shares
whether a shared value is a known hub

label: For "Duplicate Listing Detection Across Portals": Identify the same property listed by several agents and portals so search shows one entry and statistics count it once. Define the label exactly as in milestone M1: what counts as a positive or a correct outcome, and when it becomes known. Design around this trap first: Labelled pairs are easy cases chosen by reviewers, so the test overstates accuracy on hard pairs.
